content: Erythromycin is a macrolide antibiotic that is used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It may also be prescribed to prevent certain bacterial infections. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. To use erythromycin, take it orally as directed by your doctor, usually before a meal. It is best absorbed on an empty stomach. Do not crush the medication, as it has a bitter taste; swallow it whole. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using it to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow the infection to return. If you are taking it to prevent an infection, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Common side effects of erythromycin include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain or cramping, and loss of appetite. Taking the medication with food may help reduce these symptoms. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, erythromycin may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before taking erythromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (such as azithromycin or clarithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Erythromycin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are using certain medications (such as diuretics) or have conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Erythromycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Some erythromycin products may contain sodium, which should be considered if you are on a sodium-restricted diet. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Erythromycin can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting how they work. It may also interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine tests, leading to false results. In case of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store erythromycin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
